en: We must finish this work before Friday.
context: Reminding the team about a firm deadline.
explain: 'Must' shows something very important or necessary.
usage: Use it when a deadline is fixed and the whole team needs to hurry.
leelaQ: What must you finish this week?
answer: I must finish my pending tasks and send them to my manager.

en: Good work, everyone, we reached our target.
context: Thanking the team after a successful month.
explain: 'Reached our target' is a common phrase for completing a goal.
usage: Use it as a manager or senior to thank the team after a success.
leelaQ: How do you celebrate with your team?
answer: We usually have tea together and share some sweets.

en: Which task should I do first?
context: Asking a manager how to set priorities.
explain: 'Which' is used when there are a few known choices.
usage: Use it with a manager when you have many pending tasks.
leelaQ: How do you decide which task to do first?
answer: I do the urgent and important task first.

en: I have already sent you two reminders.
context: Politely telling someone you waited for a reply.
explain: 'Already' shows that it happened before now and a bit more than expected.
usage: Use it politely with a colleague who has not replied to your emails.
leelaQ: What do you do if someone does not reply to your email?
answer: I send a polite reminder and then I call them.

en: Can you please join the call on time?
tamil: தயவுசெஞ்சு சரியான நேரத்துக்கு காலுக்கு வர முடியுமா?
context: Asking a teammate to be punctual.
explain: 'Please' in the middle makes it a gentle request.
usage: Use it as a team lead when people join meetings late.
leelaQ: Why is it important to be on time?
answer: It shows respect and saves everyone's time.

en: Please do not share this file outside the team.
context: Giving a warning about a confidential file.
explain: 'Please do not' is a polite and firm order.
usage: Use it when you send private office documents to your colleagues.
leelaQ: What office files should you keep private?
answer: Salary details and client data should stay private.

en: Can we start the meeting now?
context: Asking in a meeting room when everyone is ready.
explain: 'Can we' is a friendly way to suggest an action together.
usage: Use it as an organiser when you see all people have arrived.
leelaQ: How do you start a meeting?
answer: I greet everyone and say what we will discuss today.

en: Can you give me some feedback on my work?
tamil: என் வேலைக்கு கொஞ்சம் ஃபீட்பேக் கொடுக்க முடியுமா?
context: Asking a senior to review your work.
explain: 'Some feedback' is correct. 'Feedbacks' is not used in standard English.
usage: Use it with a senior when you want to improve your work.
leelaQ: Who do you ask for feedback?
answer: I ask my team lead because he knows my work well.

en: The design team is waiting for our approval.
tamil: டிசைன் டீம் நம்ம ஒப்புதலுக்காக காத்துக்கிட்டு இருக்காங்க.
context: Reminding your manager about a pending approval.
explain: 'Is waiting for' needs 'for' before the thing you wait for.
usage: Use it when work is stopped because someone has not approved it yet.
leelaQ: What is the last thing you waited for at work?
answer: I waited for my manager's approval on a leave request.

en: When will the report be ready?
context: Asking a colleague about the time of a report.
explain: 'When will' asks about a future time.
usage: Use it when you are waiting for a document from a teammate.
leelaQ: When do you expect your next big task to finish?
answer: I expect to finish it by the end of next week.

en: Our boss appreciated the team's effort.
context: Telling your family about a good day at work.
explain: 'Appreciated' is a stronger word than 'liked'. It shows respect for hard work.
usage: Use it with friends or family when you share how the boss reacted.
leelaQ: Does your boss appreciate your work?
answer: Yes, he often says thank you after a project.

en: Please mute your mic when you are not speaking.
tamil: பேசாத நேரத்துல உங்க மைக்கை மியூட் பண்ணுங்க.
context: Reminding people in an online meeting.
explain: 'Mute' means to turn off the sound. 'When' joins the request to the condition.
usage: Use it as a host in an online meeting when there is background noise.
leelaQ: Why should you mute your mic in a call?
answer: Because the background noise disturbs the speaker.

en: I'll make the changes and send it again.
context: Replying to a reviewer after getting comments.
explain: 'I'll' is the short form of 'I will'. It is natural in spoken English.
usage: Use it when your manager or client gives you comments on your work.
leelaQ: What do you do after you get comments on your work?
answer: I read them carefully, make the changes and send it again.

en: The team worked late to meet the deadline.
tamil: டெட்லைனை எட்டுறதுக்கு டீம் லேட்டா வரைக்கும் வேலை பண்ணுச்சு.
context: Telling a friend how hard the team worked.
explain: 'To meet the deadline' means to finish the work on time.
usage: Use it when you describe a busy week to friends or to your manager.
leelaQ: Have you ever worked late for a deadline?
answer: Yes, I worked until nine o'clock to finish a report.

en: Everyone in our team helps each other.
tamil: எங்க டீம்ல எல்லாரும் ஒருத்தருக்கொருத்தர் உதவி பண்ணுவாங்க.
context: Describing your team spirit in an interview or chat.
explain: 'Each other' is used when two or more people do the same thing to one another.
usage: Use it in an interview or with a friend when you talk about your team.
leelaQ: How is the teamwork in your office?
answer: Our teamwork is good, and everyone helps when someone is busy.

en: I completed the testing yesterday.
context: Giving a status update to your team lead.
explain: 'Completed' is past tense. 'Yesterday' tells us the work was finished before today.
usage: Use it in a daily update when you report work you have already finished.
leelaQ: What work did you finish yesterday?
answer: I finished the testing and wrote a short report yesterday.

en: What is the deadline for this task?
context: Asking your manager about the last date.
explain: 'What is the ... for' is a clear question for details.
usage: Use it when you get a new task and need to know the due date.
leelaQ: What do you ask when you get a new task?
answer: I ask the deadline and who will check the work.

en: I did not understand the last point.
context: Asking politely for clarity in a meeting.
explain: 'Did not' with the base verb makes a past negative.
usage: Use it in a meeting before you ask the speaker to explain again.
leelaQ: What do you do when you do not understand something?
answer: I ask the person to explain it once more.

en: The report is not ready yet.
context: Replying to a manager who asks for the report.
explain: 'Not ready yet' means it will be ready later.
usage: Use it when a manager asks for something before you have finished.
leelaQ: What do you say when your work is not ready?
answer: I say it is not ready yet and tell them when it will be.

en: I will update the status sheet after lunch.
tamil: மதிய சாப்பாட்டுக்கு அப்புறம் ஸ்டேட்டஸ் ஷீட்டை அப்டேட் பண்றேன்.
context: Telling a teammate when you will fill the tracker.
explain: 'After lunch' is a simple time phrase for a plan.
usage: Use it with a team lead who asks for an updated tracker.
leelaQ: What do you do after lunch at work?
answer: I answer my emails and continue with my tasks.

en: Kindly reply to this mail as soon as possible.
tamil: இந்த மெயிலுக்கு முடிஞ்சவரைக்கும் சீக்கிரம் பதில் சொல்லுங்க.
context: Writing a formal email to a client.
explain: 'Kindly' is common in Indian official English. 'As soon as possible' means quickly.
usage: Use it in an email when you need a fast answer from someone.
leelaQ: How do you ask for a quick reply in an email?
answer: I write please reply as soon as possible, and I say thank you.

en: I think we should try a different approach.
tamil: நாம வேற மாதிரி முயற்சி பண்ணலாம்னு நினைக்கிறேன்.
context: Suggesting a new way to solve a problem.
explain: 'I think we should' is a soft way to give a suggestion.
usage: Use it in a team discussion when the current plan is not working.
leelaQ: How do you suggest a new idea to your team?
answer: I say I think we should try a different way.

en: I was in a client call when you messaged.
tamil: நீங்க மெசேஜ் பண்ணப்போ நான் கிளையன்ட் காலுல இருந்தேன்.
context: Explaining why you replied late.
explain: 'Was' with 'when' shows what you were doing at that time.
usage: Use it when a colleague asks why you did not reply on time.
leelaQ: Why do people reply late to messages?
answer: Maybe they are in a meeting or busy with another task.

en: Someone has to talk to the client today.
context: Pushing the team to take responsibility.
explain: 'Has to' shows that something is necessary. 'Someone' takes a singular verb.
usage: Use it in a team chat when a task needs an owner.
leelaQ: Who talks to the client in your team?
answer: Our team lead talks to the client most of the time.

en: I will check with the team and get back to you.
context: Replying to a client when you do not know the answer yet.
explain: 'Get back to you' means to reply later with the answer. It is very common at work.
usage: Use it with a client or manager when you need time to find the answer.
leelaQ: What do you say when you do not know the answer?
answer: I say I will check and get back to them soon.
